decisions.reason: The existing MODIFY captures the length clarification but leaves the prior marginal-softening constraint stale; the client now requires only an exceptionally subtle reduction in corner sharpness.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi [FREELANCER_NAME_001],

Thank you once more for preparing these. I greatly appreciate the methodical way you have handled every round. It has made the process considerably easier, and I honestly believe we have reached the final refinements.

After reviewing the results for some time, I realized that my use of the word "reach" may have accidentally created ambiguity. What I intended to describe was much more mechanical than expressive.

My request for additional reach in Variation 1 was actually a request for a tiny increase in the right arm’s length, with the existing Option B terminal left completely untouched. In retrospect, "length" would have communicated my intention much more accurately than "reach."

Since the terminal itself changed in Variation 1, I cannot easily assess the single variable I wanted to examine. My goal was to compare the original Option B against another version that differed only through a very slight lengthening of the right arm.

For the next study, I’d like to structure the exploration as follows:

1. Begin with the original Option B and increase only the right arm’s length by a very small amount. Do not alter its terminal geometry, taper, point shape, or profile. It should look as though the existing arm simply continues a little farther along precisely the same line before terminating. Apply this identical adjustment to the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

The horizontal reference line was extremely useful, so please retain it in this comparison.

2. Use that longer Option B version, preserve exactly the same added length, and soften the terminal only very slightly. I do not want more curvature or a flourish, merely a gentler finish that retains the same architectural language. The tip must remain straight, with only an exceptionally subtle reduction in the sharpness of its corners.

3. Apply that same small length increase to Option C while leaving its current terminal personality and overall geometry untouched. Again, use the treatment consistently for the Hero V, second V, and É accent.

I think Variations 2 and 3 successfully investigated the softer terminal language. The difficulty is that both originated from a Variation 1 terminal that had already been modified, making it hard to distinguish the effect of added length from the effect of a redesigned terminal.

At this stage, I feel we are testing one variable at a time. The finish, spacing, slope, proportions, and overall architecture all seem locked. I am only trying to decide whether a slightly longer right arm strengthens the logo further, and then whether its terminal should remain precisely unchanged or be softened by just a touch.

Thank you again for the care you have brought to this work. We are extraordinarily close, and I sincerely appreciate your patience while we investigate these last nuances.

value_updates.length_adjustment: Apply the same very small length increase used for the Hero V and second V while continuing the existing form along the same line.
value_updates.terminal_treatment: For the Option B length comparison, preserve the original terminal geometry, taper, point shape, and profile unchanged.
value_updates.derivation_method: Literal extraction of the refined Option B terminal section of the Hero V's right arm, including the same very small length increase produced by continuing the arm along the same line.
value_updates.required_correspondence: Apply the identical very small right-arm length increase to the É accent while preserving the original Option B terminal geometry, taper, point shape, and profile; any softened comparison must retain the same added length and straight tip.
value_updates.terminal_softness_constraint: Any softened comparison must add no curvature or flourish, retain a straight tip and the same added length, and reduce corner sharpness only exceptionally slightly.

decisions.reason: The existing MODIFY correctly isolates length but fails to update the prior marginal-softening constraint to the explicitly narrower exceptionally subtle corner treatment.
